content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine). In retrosynthesis, we need to break them in reverse order: target -> break amide to give acid + aniline; then break alkene to give aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner gives α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid. Then sulfonamide formation: sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + amine. So we need to propose precursors: For target, we have sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: one ring with methyl (toluene) attached to sulfonamide nitrogen; other ring with sulfonyl attached to aromatic ring bearing the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus retrosynthetic steps:

Step1 (reverse amide coupling): break C(=O)N to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: /C=C/C(=O) (attached to aromatic ring) i.e., the side chain attached to aromatic ring c2ccc(... )cc2. The amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Wait the acid is attached to aromatic ring via the double bond: the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... In reverse, we have /C=C/COOH attached to aromatic ring. So precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (the acid). Precursor B: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to the aniline, so the amine is aniline (para? not substituted). So we have aniline.

Step2 (reverse Doebner): The unsaturated acid (with double bond) derived from aldehyde + malonic acid. So break the double bond to give aldehyde attached to aromatic ring (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonyl group? Wait the aldehyde is on the same aromatic ring that later becomes the unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl. So we need aromatic aldehyde: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (with sulfonyl attached). So precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1 (aryl aldehyde). And malonic acid.

Step3 (reverse sulfonamide formation): The sulfonamide linking the toluene ring nitrogen to sulfonyl chloride. So break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) and aniline (the toluene ring with NH2). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the toluene ring (para-methyl phenyl) as an aniline. So precursor: p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1 and sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-aryl where aryl is the other aromatic ring (the one bearing aldehyde). So sulfonyl chloride: Cl[S](=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2.

Thus overall three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with nested reactions.

We need template IDs for each step. We have search results earlier: template 733 seems to be sulfonamide formation (ClSO2-aryl + aniline -> sulfonamide). That matches our step3. So we can use template_id 733.

For amide coupling, need template that forms amide from acid and amine. Search for amide formation. Let's search.
